validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: this is not a GEM-only entity. Independently confirmed via FERC's own Federal Register docket CP10-459-000 for the 'ETC Tiger Pipeline Expansion Project-Phase I' -- Notice of Application (75 FR 38799, published 2010-07-06) states ETC Tiger Pipeline, LLC (a subsidiary of Energy Transfer Partners, L.P.) filed on June 15, 2010 under NGA sec. 7(c) 'requesting: (1) Authorization to construct, own, operate and maintain approximately 20.5 miles of 42-inch diameter natural gas pipeline and 30,565 horsepower of compression located in Louisiana capable of transporting up to 400,000 Mcf/day (Expansion Project)'. The companion Notice of Intent to prepare an EA (75 FR 51033, published 2010-08-18) itemizes the construction: 'Loop 1 -- approximately 8.2 miles of new 42-inch diameter loop in Bienville Parish, Louisiana; and Loop 2 -- approximately 12.3 miles of new 42-inch diameter pipeline in Jackson and Ouachita Parishes, LA' plus added compression at Cannisnia (Red River Parish), Bienville, and Chatham (Jackson Parish) compressor stations, and states 'The Project would add 0.4 billion cubic feet/day of natural gas capacity to Tiger's system.' 8.2+12.3=20.5 mi -- GEM's LengthKnown=21.00 mi is within normal rounding. A second, fully independent origin (the industry project database offshore-technology.com, formerly hydrocarbons-technology.com -- same underlying page, redirected) corroborates from outside the FERC docket: 'The estimated cost of the expansion was $193m' (matches GEM SegmentCost=193,000,000 USD exactly), 'the extended pipeline has a capacity of 400,000mcf per day' (matches GEM Capacity=400.00 MMcf/d exactly, and independently confirms the FERC application's own figure), diameter 42 inches (matches), and 'The expansion project was submitted for approval to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission in June 2010 and was given certificate order in February 2011' (matches the FERC docket's June 2010 filing date; explains GEM's ConstructionYear=2011/StartYear1=2011 -- construction followed the Feb-2011 certificate, and the page separately notes the full system reached 2.4 Bcf/d, up from the original 2.0 Bcf/d, by August 2011, i.e. after this expansion entered service). No exact construction/in-service MONTH is stated anywhere I could reach this session, so Construction/Start stay at year-only confidence (medium-high) rather than high. CLASSIFICATION: correctly 'transmission' -- an FERC-jurisdictional NGA sec. 7(c) interstate certificate project, not a gathering/process line. DUPLICATE: checked against all 36 other rows in the 37-pipeline roster -- no match. Note for the record (not a duplicate flag, since no roster PID exists to name): the parent ~175-195-mile Carthage TX-to-Louisiana Tiger mainline (FERC Docket CP09-460, per Natural Gas Intelligence's 2010-02-02 environmental-nod article, and Energy Transfer Partners' 2009-02-20 open-season release, both read in full) is NOT itself a row in this 50-pipeline batch/roster -- it may be tracked under a different PID outside this Gulf Coast slice (e.g. the Texas batch, since its Texas terminus at Panola County/Carthage Hub would route there) or may not be tracked as its own GEM entity at all. Flagging for the orchestrator's awareness only; not enough information from this roster to call it Discovery or duplicate. The FERC docket places the ENTIRE expansion (both loops + all three compressor-station upgrades) in Bienville, Jackson, Ouachita, and Red River Parishes -- all Louisiana, no Texas leg -- so StartState/Province should also read 'Louisiana', not stay blank (fill below). SPEC: Length, Diameter, Capacity, Construction/Start-year all confirmed as above. SegmentCost=193,000,000 USD is corroborated in only ONE place I could verify (offshore-technology.com) -- the FERC Notice of Application and the EA-scoping notice (both read to exhaustion) do not state a cost estimate; the actual FERC certificate order (which likely would) sits behind elibrary.ferc.gov's JS-rendered search, not reachable via curl this session, and both DuckDuckGo (returned HTTP 202, bot-challenge) and Bing (returned no scrapeable result body) failed to surface a second source, and the WebSearch tool had already exhausted its session-wide budget (200/200) by the time I reached this cell. SegmentCost therefore stays supported at medium tier pending that second origin -- flagging rather than force-closing it. CITATION-POOL ACCOUNTING: the wiki page harvested 6 citations.
